description: R08 Host InputBuffer portable queue/coalescing checkpoint: safe Rust owns 19 of 20 Microsoft InputBufferTests contracts across insertion, coalescing, flush/read/peek, wait signaling, prepend/reinitialize, pause handling and stream de-coalescing. The CP_JAPANESE DBCS conversion contract remains Missing because actual Windows codepage conversion is still a platform responsibility.

entries.notes: Single writes increase the ready-event count and mixed key/menu storage reports the exact queue size.
Twelve individual writes preserve each event at the back of storage and report twelve ready events.
Bulk insertion preserves all twelve menu records without individual-write coalescing.
Consecutive MOUSE_MOVED events coalesce to the latest position, while an intervening key breaks coalescing.
A bulk mouse batch is appended verbatim even after a prior single mouse event.
Identical single key writes coalesce into one event whose repeat count equals the number of writes.
Bulk key insertion bypasses coalescing and preserves all records individually.
UTF-16 surrogate code units never coalesce, including repeated low-surrogate events.
Flush clears all queued input and resets ready-event state.
FlushAllButKeys removes non-key records while preserving all key records in order.
Normal reads return queued records in FIFO order and consume the requested records.
Peek returns the same FIFO records without consuming storage.
Consuming only part of the queue leaves the wait event signaled; consuming the remainder resets it.
Prepend places a complete batch before existing records while preserving order within both batches.
Reinitialize restores the default input mode and empties queued state.
Pause suspends output and is discarded; the next ordinary key resumes output and is also discarded.
Modifier/system keys remain queued while output is suspended and do not resume the console.
Stream reads emit one repeat while decrementing the stored repeat count in place.
Stream peeks emit one repeat without mutating the stored coalesced repeat count.
